reference: Values are gameplay-tuned from public mission datasheets. Dimensions in metres. Mass in kg. Cost in USD.

parts.name: Rutherford Cluster (3x)
parts.description: Three small electric-pump-fed kerolox engines. Light, restartable, and the bottom end of the orbital launch market.
parts.heritage: Based on Rocket Lab Electron first stage.

parts.name: Light Thrust Structure
parts.description: A composite truss for small launch vehicles. Carries the engine load into the tank walls.
parts.heritage: Based on Electron and LauncherOne thrust structures.

parts.name: RP-1 Tank (Small)
parts.description: A small kerosene tank for lightweight vehicles. Same fuel as the big rockets, half the mass.
parts.heritage: Based on small launch vehicle tankage.

parts.name: LOX Tank (Small)
parts.description: A small liquid oxygen tank. Same cryogenic handling as the larger LOX tanks, less propellant.
parts.heritage: Based on small launch vehicle tankage.

parts.name: Light Intertank
parts.description: A small intertank structure for lightweight two-stage vehicles.
parts.heritage: Based on Electron and Firefly Alpha intertanks.

parts.name: Small Interstage
parts.description: A lightweight interstage for small two-stage vehicles. Jettisoned at separation.
parts.heritage: Based on Electron and Rocket 3 interstages.

parts.name: Standard Nose Cone
parts.description: A simple ogive shape that covers the payload during ascent. Jettisoned once above the atmosphere.
parts.heritage: Flown on nearly every atmospheric launch vehicle since the 1950s.

parts.name: Reinforced Nose Cone
parts.description: Thicker skin and a heat-resistant cap for launches that pass through denser atmosphere or higher dynamic pressure.
parts.heritage: Common on vehicles flying heavy payloads through max-Q.

parts.name: Sensor Nose Cone
parts.description: Carries a small instrument package behind a transparent window in the tip. Adds a camera or probe ahead of the main payload.
parts.heritage: Flown on atmospheric probe missions and upper stage test flights.

parts.name: Apollo-Class Guidance Unit
parts.description: A flight computer, inertial measurement unit, and star tracker in a single box. The entry-level option for steering and navigation.
parts.heritage: Heritage design pattern from Apollo and Shuttle-era flight computers.

parts.name: Rad-Hard Flight Computer
parts.description: Hardened against ionising radiation. Required for missions to Jupiter's belts or long-duration inner solar system flights.
parts.heritage: Flown on Juno, Europa Clipper, and every mission past the asteroid belt.

parts.name: Autonomy Package
parts.description: Onboard software and additional processors that let the spacecraft handle known faults without waiting for commands from Earth.
parts.heritage: Based on Deep Space 1's Remote Agent and later autonomy research.

parts.name: Camera Suite
parts.description: A multi-spectral imaging system. Low mass, low power, and the workhorse instrument on most flyby missions.
parts.heritage: Based on Mastcam-Z (Perseverance) and LORRI (New Horizons).

parts.name: Mass Spectrometer
parts.description: Analyses the chemical composition of gases and surface material. Detects organic molecules at parts-per-billion sensitivity.

parts.name: Drill and Sample Cache
parts.description: Rotary percussive drill with a sealed sample container. Required for any mission that returns material to Earth.
parts.heritage: Based on Curiosity and Perseverance sampling systems.

parts.name: Ground-Penetrating Radar
parts.description: Maps subsurface ice and rock layers from orbit or a flyby. The primary tool for studying icy moons.

parts.name: Magnetometer Boom
parts.description: A long boom that holds a magnetic field sensor away from the spacecraft's own electronics. Cheap and scientifically useful.
parts.heritage: Flown on Voyager, Galileo, Juno, and most outer planet missions.

parts.name: Solar Array (Small)
parts.description: A single deployable solar panel. Output scales with distance from the Sun, so it is only practical inside the asteroid belt.
parts.heritage: Standard on inner solar system satellites.

parts.name: Solar Array (Large)
parts.description: A pair of large deployable wings with higher output. Same distance limitation as the small array but four times the power.
parts.heritage: Based on Juno's three-wing configuration and Psyche's solar arrays.

parts.name: RTG (Pu-238)
parts.description: Radioisotope thermoelectric generator. Converts heat from plutonium decay into electricity. Works anywhere, but the supply of Pu-238 is limited.
parts.heritage: Voyager, Cassini, New Horizons, Curiosity, Perseverance.

parts.name: Battery Pack
parts.description: Stores energy for eclipse periods and high-power manoeuvres. Required with solar arrays because panels produce nothing at night.
parts.heritage: Li-ion chemistry based on Mars rover and ISS batteries.

parts.name: Upper Stage Tank (Small)
parts.description: High-efficiency propellant tank for the upper stage. Light and compact.
parts.heritage: Based on Centaur and Falcon 9 second stage tank designs.

parts.name: Upper Stage Tank (Large)
parts.description: A larger upper stage tank for missions that need more delta-V after stage separation.
parts.heritage: Based on Centaur III and Ariane 5 ESC-A upper stages.

parts.name: Vacuum Engine (Small)
parts.description: A vacuum-optimised engine with a large nozzle for high specific impulse. Useless at sea level.

parts.name: Vacuum Engine (Large)
parts.description: A high-thrust vacuum engine for heavy payloads. Better efficiency and higher thrust than the small version.
parts.heritage: Based on RL10B-2 and Vinci engines.

parts.name: Pyrotechnic Separation
parts.description: Explosive bolts and springs that push the two stages apart. Proven, cheap, one-shot.
parts.heritage: Standard on every multistage rocket since the 1950s.

parts.name: Hot-Stage Ring
parts.description: The upper stage ignites while still attached. No springs, no pyros, just thrust pushing the stages apart. Reusable, but the interstage must be vented.
parts.heritage: Based on Starship hot-staging and Soviet-era designs.

parts.name: Standard Interstage
parts.description: A light structural cylinder that connects the first and second stages. Jettisoned at separation.

parts.name: Heavy Interstage
parts.description: A reinforced interstage for high-mass upper stages or hot-staging. Carries more load but weighs more.
parts.heritage: Based on heavy lift interstage structures.

parts.name: Grid Fins (Small)
parts.description: Titanium lattice fins that steer the vehicle during atmospheric ascent. Deployed after max-Q.

parts.name: Grid Fins (Large)
parts.description: Larger control surfaces for heavier vehicles flying through thicker atmosphere.

parts.name: Pressurant System
parts.description: Helium composite-overwrapped pressure vessels and regulators that keep the tanks pressurised as propellant drains.
parts.heritage: Standard on all liquid propellant rockets.

parts.name: Autogenous Pressurisation
parts.description: Taps hot gas from the engine to pressurise the tanks. Eliminates helium but requires more engine complexity.

parts.name: Intertank Structure
parts.description: A composite cylinder that connects the fuel and oxidizer tanks and carries structural loads between them.

parts.name: Heavy Intertank
parts.description: Reinforced intertank for heavy lift vehicles. Carries more axial load and supports larger tanks.

parts.name: RP-1 Kerosene Tank
parts.description: Refined kerosene. Dense, storable, and well understood. The workhorse fuel of the last sixty years.
parts.heritage: Falcon 9, Saturn V first stage, Soyuz.

parts.name: Liquid Methane Tank
parts.description: Liquid methane. Cleaner burning than kerosene, easier to store than hydrogen, and manufacturable on Mars from local CO2 and water.
parts.heritage: Starship, Raptor engines, Blue Origin BE-4.

parts.name: Liquid Hydrogen Tank
parts.description: Liquid hydrogen. The highest specific impulse of any practical chemical fuel, but very low density and it boils off over time.
parts.heritage: SLS core stage, Centaur, Ariane 5 ECA.

parts.name: LOX Tank
parts.description: Liquid oxygen. The standard oxidiser for almost every liquid rocket. Non-toxic, but it boils off over days to weeks.

parts.name: N2O4 Tank
parts.description: Nitrogen tetroxide. Hypergolic with hydrazine, storable at room temperature, and used for decades on deep space probes.
parts.heritage: Cassini, Voyager, most deep space missions.

parts.name: Standard Thrust Structure
parts.description: A truss assembly that distributes engine thrust into the tank walls. Without it, the engines rip free of the tank.

parts.name: Heavy Thrust Structure
parts.description: Reinforced thrust structure for high-thrust or high-mass first stages.

parts.name: Merlin Cluster (9x)
parts.description: Nine sea-level kerolox engines arranged in an octaweb. High thrust, restartable, and one of the most reliable engine configurations in service.

parts.name: RS-25 Cluster (4x)
parts.description: Four hydrogen-oxygen engines adapted from the Space Shuttle main engines. Extremely high specific impulse but requires liquid hydrogen.

parts.name: Raptor Cluster (3x)
parts.description: Three full-flow staged combustion methalox engines. High thrust, high efficiency, and designed for reuse.

parts.name: Small Solid Booster
parts.description: A small strap-on solid rocket. Adds thrust at liftoff and is jettisoned a few minutes later.

parts.name: Large Liquid Booster
parts.description: A large strap-on booster with its own liquid engine. More thrust than solid, and can be throttled.

parts.name: Reaction Control System
parts.description: A cluster of small thrusters that orient the spacecraft in vacuum. Required for any attitude change after the main engine shuts down.

parts.name: RD-180 (2 chambers)
parts.description: A dual-chamber kerolox engine derived from the Soviet RD-170. Very high thrust in a compact envelope.
parts.heritage: Atlas V first stage, 2000 to present.

parts.name: BE-4 Cluster (2x)
parts.description: Two methalox engines with oxygen-rich staged combustion. Designed for reuse and high thrust.

parts.name: Solid Motor Cluster (4x)
parts.description: Four strap-on solid motors. Simple, cheap, reliable, and cannot be throttled or shut down once lit.

parts.name: Nuclear Thermal (NERVA-class)
parts.description: A nuclear thermal rocket. Hydrogen is heated by a fission reactor and expelled at very high velocity. Isp roughly double any chemical engine.

parts.name: Composite Thrust Structure
parts.description: Carbon fiber reinforced polymer thrust frame. Lighter than aluminum at the same strength.

parts.name: Titanium Thrust Structure
parts.description: Titanium frame. Higher temperature tolerance than aluminum for high-thrust applications.

parts.name: Methane Tank (Small)
parts.description: A compact methane tank. Same clean-burning fuel as the large methalox tanks, half the mass.

parts.name: Stainless Balloon Tank
parts.description: Very thin stainless steel. Pressurised to hold its shape. Extremely light for its volume, but the pressure must never fail.

parts.name: Hydrogen Peroxide Tank
parts.description: High-test peroxide. Storable, non-cryogenic, and decomposes cleanly into steam and oxygen. Lower performance than LOX.
parts.heritage: Soyuz RCS, Blue Origin New Shepard, British Black Arrow.

parts.name: Nitrous Oxide Tank
parts.description: Self-pressurising oxidiser. Simple plumbing, no helium needed, used by small launchers and hybrid motors.
parts.heritage: Virgin Galactic SpaceShipTwo, hybrid test rockets.

parts.name: Composite Intertank
parts.description: Carbon fiber intertank. Half the mass of the aluminum version with higher stiffness.

parts.name: High Pressure Helium (COPV)
parts.description: A cluster of high-pressure composite overwrapped pressure vessels. More helium capacity than the standard system.

parts.name: Titanium Grid Fins
parts.description: Titanium lattice fins. The original design used on Falcon 9. Withstands higher heat loads than aluminum.

parts.name: Composite Grid Fins
parts.description: Lightweight composite control surfaces. Cheaper than titanium and lighter, but with lower heat tolerance.

parts.name: Composite Interstage
parts.description: Carbon fiber interstage. Lighter than aluminum, jettisoned after stage separation.

parts.name: Marman Clamp Separation
parts.description: A clamp band that holds the stages together and releases with a single pyro cutter. Standard on most modern rockets.

parts.name: Frangible Ring Separation
parts.description: A ring with a shaped charge that splits cleanly when fired. Used on solid stages and small launchers.

parts.name: RL10
parts.description: The most-flown hydrogen upper stage engine in history. Restartable, extremely efficient, and used on every Centaur upper stage since 1963.

parts.name: Vinci
parts.description: A European expander-cycle hydrogen engine. Higher thrust than RL10 with similar efficiency.

parts.name: Raptor Vacuum
parts.description: A methalox vacuum engine with a large expansion ratio nozzle. Full-flow staged combustion.

parts.name: Upper Stage Tank (XL)
parts.description: A very large upper stage tank for high-delta-V missions or heavy payloads.
parts.heritage: Based on Starship and SLS Exploration Upper Stage tankage.

parts.name: Upper Stage Tank (Methane)
parts.description: Methalox upper stage tank. Higher density than hydrogen, no boil-off problems, moderate efficiency.

parts.name: Star Tracker Assembly
parts.description: A high-accuracy optical navigation unit. Determines orientation by imaging known stars. Required for deep space missions with long light delay.
parts.heritage: Based on Juno and Voyager star trackers.

parts.name: Deep Space Transponder
parts.description: X-band and Ka-band radio for communicating across the solar system. Compatible with NASA's Deep Space Network.

parts.name: Solar Array (XL)
parts.description: Four huge deployable wings. The largest solar power system ever flown. Total output similar to a small house.
parts.heritage: Based on the ISS main solar arrays scaled for interplanetary use.

parts.name: MMRTG
parts.description: Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator. The standard nuclear power source for outer solar system missions since 2011.

parts.name: Kilopower Fission Reactor
parts.description: A small fission reactor using uranium-235. Delivers 10 kW for 15 years. Far more power than an RTG, but heavier and politically sensitive.
parts.heritage: NASA Kilopower Reactor Using Stirling Technology (KRUSTY), ground tests 2018.

parts.name: Battery Pack (Large)
parts.description: A high-capacity Li-ion battery. Stores enough energy for a full eclipse period or a major manoeuvre.
parts.heritage: Based on ISS and deep space mission battery designs.

parts.name: High-Resolution Camera
parts.description: A triplet of high-resolution cameras with independent focal lengths. Returns detailed surface imagery at multiple wavelengths.

parts.name: Infrared Camera
parts.description: Thermal infrared imager. Maps surface temperature and detects buried ice.

parts.name: UV Spectrometer
parts.description: Ultraviolet spectrometer. Maps atmospheric ozone and identifies minerals on the surface.

parts.name: Gamma Ray Spectrometer
parts.description: Detects gamma rays emitted by radioactive elements on the surface. Maps the elemental composition of a planet.

parts.name: Synthetic Aperture Radar
parts.description: An imaging radar that can see through clouds and dust. Very high power draw, very high data return.

parts.name: Weather Station
parts.description: Temperature, pressure, wind, and humidity sensors mounted on a small mast. The standard lander science suite.

parts.name: Seismometer
parts.description: Detects ground motion from marsquakes, meteorite impacts, and internal activity. Requires precise levelling.
parts.heritage: InSight SEIS, Apollo Passive Seismic Network.

parts.name: Deep Drill + Analyzer
parts.description: A two-metre drill that can reach below the oxidised surface layer. Includes an onboard lab to analyse cores. The most scientifically valuable instrument on any surface mission.
parts.heritage: ExoMars Rosalind Franklin drill, proposed Mars Sample Return.

parts.name: Sample Return Capsule
parts.description: A sealed capsule with an ablative heat shield that carries collected samples back to Earth. Requires a drill elsewhere on the spacecraft.

parts.name: Small Rover
parts.description: A six-wheeled rover that deploys after landing. Can travel kilometres and sample multiple sites.

parts.name: Von Karman Nose Cone
parts.description: A mathematically optimised shape that minimises drag at supersonic speeds. The standard for high-performance vehicles.
parts.heritage: Terrier-Orion, Black Brant, high-speed test vehicles.

parts.name: Blunt Nose Cone
parts.description: A blunt shape for very high-speed re-entry. Distributes heat more evenly than a sharp cone.

parts.name: Ablative Aeroshell
parts.description: A heat shield for atmospheric entry. The ablative material burns away to carry heat off the payload. Required for any lander at Mars.

parts.name: Methalox Cluster (5x)
parts.description: Five methalox engines with electric ignition. Restartable, reusable, and clean-burning.
parts.heritage: Based on Raptor and BE-4 test articles.

parts.name: Hypergolic Cluster (4x)
parts.description: Four hypergolic engines. Ignite on contact, storable at room temperature, and restartable after years in space.

parts.name: Aerospike (2x)
parts.description: Two aerospike engines. Altitude-compensating nozzles maintain efficiency across the whole flight envelope, from sea level to vacuum.
parts.heritage: Experimental. Tested on the Linear Aerospike SR-71 and X-33 proposals.

parts.name: Aft Skirt with TPS
parts.description: A heavy aft skirt with thermal protection tiles. Shields the base from engine plume heating.

parts.name: Magnesium Thrust Structure
parts.description: A magnesium alloy thrust frame. Very light, but lower melting point than aluminum.

parts.name: Stainless Steel Thrust Frame
parts.description: A stainless steel frame. Higher temperature tolerance, more mass than aluminum.

parts.name: Methane Tank (XL)
parts.description: A very large methane tank for super-heavy vehicles. Provides massive delta-V in a single stack.

parts.name: Storable Hydrazine Tank
parts.description: Hydrazine monopropellant. Storable for decades, no cryogenic handling, but lower performance.
parts.heritage: Cassini, Voyager, most deep space missions.

parts.name: LOX Tank (Large)
parts.description: A large liquid oxygen tank for heavy-lift first stages. Requires active cryo management.

parts.name: Mixed Oxides of Nitrogen Tank
parts.description: MON-3 mixed oxides. Storable, high-performance, hypergolic with hydrazine.

parts.name: Titanium Intertank
parts.description: A titanium intertank section. Higher heat tolerance than composite, lighter than stainless.

parts.name: Composite Intertank (XL)
parts.description: A very large composite intertank for super-heavy vehicles.

parts.name: Regenerative Pressurant
parts.description: Taps hot gas from the engine cooling jacket to pressurise the tanks. No helium needed. Requires engine support.

parts.name: Nitrogen Pressurant
parts.description: Cheap nitrogen gas bottles. Heavier than helium for the same pressure but universally available.
parts.heritage: Soviet-era rockets, some modern small launchers.

parts.name: Aluminum Grid Fins
parts.description: Aluminum alloy grid fins. Cheap and light, but they soften at high re-entry temperatures.

parts.name: Folding Grid Fins
parts.description: Grid fins that fold flat against the booster during launch. Reduces drag and protects them from aero loads.

parts.name: Titanium Interstage
parts.description: A titanium interstage. Higher heat tolerance for re-entry scenarios.

parts.name: Stretched Interstage
parts.description: An extended interstage that carries additional equipment or a larger upper stage tank.

parts.name: Pneumatic Separation System
parts.description: Compressed gas pistons push the stages apart. Reusable, no pyrotechnics, but slower than pyro.

parts.name: Zero-Zero Separation System
parts.description: Provides zero relative velocity and zero tip-off at separation. Used for high-precision payload deployment.
parts.heritage: ULA payload attach fittings, precision satellite deployment.

parts.name: Methalox Upper Engine
parts.description: A methane-oxygen upper stage engine. Higher density propellant than hydrogen, easier to handle, moderate efficiency.
parts.heritage: Based on Raptor Vacuum and BE-3U.

parts.name: Hypergolic Upper Engine
parts.description: A storable hypergolic upper stage engine. Restartable after years of coast.
parts.heritage: Apollo Service Propulsion System, Cassini main engine.

parts.name: Long Duration Upper Tank
parts.description: An upper stage tank with active cryo-cooling for multi-year coast phases. Required for outer planet missions.
parts.heritage: Based on Centaur long-duration variants and proposed cryo stages.

parts.name: Triple-Redundant Flight Computer
parts.description: Three flight computers voting on every decision. Any one can fail without affecting the mission.

parts.name: CubeSat-Class Avionics
parts.description: A tiny integrated flight computer and IMU. Cheap, low-power, but single-string.

parts.name: Autonomous Operations Suite
parts.description: A full autonomy package with machine-learning fault detection. The spacecraft can diagnose and recover from faults without ground contact.
parts.heritage: Based on Deep Space 1 Remote Agent, AEGIS on Curiosity, and modern autonomy research.

parts.name: Solar Array (Medium)
parts.description: A pair of medium solar wings. Balanced output for inner solar system missions.

parts.name: Fuel Cell Stack
parts.description: Hydrogen-oxygen fuel cells producing electricity and water. Used on crewed missions since Gemini.

parts.name: Large Fission Reactor
parts.description: A 100 kW fission reactor. Powers entire outposts and heavy science payloads. Requires radiation shielding for the crew.
parts.heritage: Proposed for lunar and Mars surface power.

parts.name: X-Ray Spectrometer
parts.description: Measures X-ray fluorescence to identify surface elements. Detects what a rock is made of from orbit.

parts.name: Neutron Spectrometer
parts.description: Detects neutrons to map subsurface hydrogen. The standard tool for finding water ice.

parts.name: Atmospheric Sampler
parts.description: Collects and analyses atmospheric gases. Can detect trace biomarkers at parts-per-trillion sensitivity.

parts.name: LIDAR Topographic Mapper
parts.description: Laser altimeter. Maps surface elevation at centimetre precision from orbit or flyby.

parts.name: Subsurface Ice Mapper
parts.description: Combines radar and neutron detection to build a full 3D map of subsurface water ice.
parts.heritage: Based on MARSIS and the proposed International Mars Ice Mapper.

parts.name: Micro-Rover Swarm
parts.description: Four tiny rovers that deploy together and explore different sites simultaneously.
parts.heritage: Proposed for lunar and Mars exploration.

parts.name: Astrobiology Lab
parts.description: A miniaturised wet lab. Stains, images, and analyses samples for signs of past or present life.
parts.heritage: Based on proposed Mars Sample Return and Europa Lander concepts.

parts.name: Ogive Nose Cone
parts.description: A traditional ogive nose. Sharp tip, curved sides, good low-speed aerodynamics.
parts.heritage: Most sounding rockets and early launch vehicles.

parts.name: Parabolic Nose Cone
parts.description: A parabolic profile that balances drag and heat load. Used at moderate supersonic speeds.

parts.name: Bi-Conic Nose Cone
parts.description: Two cones stacked. Simple to manufacture, predictable aerodynamics at moderate speeds.

parts.name: Aeroshell (XL)
parts.description: A very large ablative aeroshell for heavy landers. Flown on every Mars surface mission to date.
